title: Coptic and Ge’ez: documented Catholic states and bounded transitions

traditions.label: Bohairic Coptic manuscript tradition
traditions.scope: Medieval Coptic witnesses to the three-anaphora Euchologion.
traditions.coverage_note: Ancestral/comparative evidence, kept distinct from demonstrably Catholic printings.

traditions.label: Coptic Catholic Euchologion
traditions.scope: Coptic and received Arabic Catholic liturgical books; 1736, 1898 and 1971 attested states.
traditions.coverage_note: Whole 1736 offered scan recovered; exact medieval exemplar, complete 1898/1971 comparison and later received-state sequence remain incomplete.

traditions.label: Ge’ez Aksumite Euchologion witness
traditions.scope: Canonical-liturgical collection UM-039 and its eucharistic texts.
traditions.coverage_note: Historical source tradition; no demonstrated modern Catholic reception or linear succession to 1945.

traditions.label: Ge’ez liturgy in the Rome 1548 printing
traditions.scope: The Ethiopian Ordo communis and anaphoras printed at Rome by Tasfa Ṣeyon with the New Testament (1548; afterword 1549).
traditions.coverage_note: Earliest printed witness of the shared Ethiopian liturgy, kept apart from the Catholic printings of 1890 onward. Printing in Rome under papal patronage is not an approval of the text or evidence of its use by any Catholic community.

traditions.label: Ge’ez Catholic missal
traditions.scope: Catholic printings of 1890, 1913, 1945 and the joint 2024 edition presented in 2025.
traditions.coverage_note: Original earlier books remain unacquired. The 2024 editorial note expressly names 1945 as the replaced edition; presentation and local implementation are separate dates.

sources.title: Raphael Tuki, Missale copto arabicum, Rome 1736; ULB Bonn digital copy
sources.inspection: Entire Bonn IIIF manifest and all 676 default JPEG images acquired, each hashed and preserved in provider order; lossless 676-page PDF derivative independently checked by recovering and byte-comparing every JPEG stream. Title, incense openings, part II pp. 3, 86–87, 110–111, 212–213, 262, 272, 277, 282, 287–290 and 317, and the final colophon inspected. Creed printed II p. 86 / artifact 379 directly includes procession from the Father and Son in Coptic and Arabic. Colophon artifact 672 gives 3 Baunah / 13 June 1736. PDF SHA-256 add039d0fa12b9379035c2820e10ff6df042dc49651628a7dc7f3e9f6b5f375f; ZIP SHA-256 a09b63688e35e0b4a372063ea1f26bdf5f990686c17358483820383f42461eed; exact manifest SHA-256 ea71e2eecf1a4183e7c69fd75a6a6e93178ded0ed8f9aaa299cc7ab78c6131c6. Complete Arabic Creed II pp. 85–87 / artifacts 378–380 independently word-checked and retained as a 139-word unvocalized reading transcription; normalized-text SHA-256 79536f9cec56d16b9a1740b9baf9db7353b435577320b60983ffa674b4f9563e. The five errata leaves, artifacts 667–671, were checked for this component; no listed correction to its Arabic words was identified.
sources.limitations: The complete offered 1000-pixel-wide image sequence is acquired; physical-volume completeness, complete transcription and whole-book collation are not established. Blue reader annotations on Basil’s cup-narrative leaves are separate from the original print. Medieval exemplar identity and a complete 1898 comparison remain unresolved. Bonn’s extent field says 288, 479 pages, which is not reconciled with the 676-image offered sequence; Part I printed p. 288 is artifact 293, errata begin at 667, and the colophon is 672.

sources.title: Testamentum Novum … Missale cum benedictione incensi cerae et c. … Fr. Petrus Ethyops … imprimi curavit (Rome: Valerius Doricus and Ludovicus, 1548; afterword dated 1549), Google Books copy jXZRAAAAcAAJ
sources.inspection: Retained 486-image roster from the 2026-10-19 Ge’ez lane (ZIP SHA-256 ae42d82db123742934aa854640f728416b4413924186ae14a18c407b51cd286c). Visually read on 2026-10-21: title PP7; Latin preface Christiano et pio lectori PP8–PP10; f. 158r headed INTROITVS MISSE with Ge’ez text; contact survey of ff. 157r–177v; headings at f. 168r (ቅዳሴ፡ እግዚእነ…), f. 170r (ቅዳሴ፡ ዘእግዝእትነ፡ ማርያም፡ ዘደረሰ፡ አባ፡ ህርያቆስ…) and the ornament band opening a further section on f. 174r; Latin printer’s colophon on f. 176v (Impressum est opus hoc Romae per Valerium Doricum & Ludovicum Fratres Brixianos, 1548); Latin afterword PT1 dated Anno Domini 1549, Ethiopian reckoning 6586, under Paul III and the Ethiopian emperor Claudius.
sources.limitations: Ge’ez text not transcribed or collated; the section beginning f. 174r was not identified. No approbation, imprimatur or statement of Roman revision of the Mass appears on the inspected leaves; the papal reign is a dating and patronage formula. A BSB stamp and a Propaganda Fide college ex libris record later ownership, not liturgical use. The Napoli copy and the 1549 Latin rendering were not examined.

stages.label: Medieval three-anaphora witness
stages.scope: Basil, Gregory and Cyril anaphoras in Vat.copt.17.
stages.summary: A dated medieval witness to the three named anaphoras; it supplies historical context for the later printed repertoire.

evidence.claim: Lists Vat.Copt.xvii with 1288 date among manuscripts containing Basil, Gregory and Cyril.
Holding-library shelfmark confirmed.

stages.limitations: No claim that this manuscript is Tuki’s direct exemplar, a Catholic book, or a complete reconstruction of thirteenth-century practice. Original folios not yet inspected.
stages.reception: Medieval Coptic witness; Catholic reception not established.

stages.label: Tuki’s Catholic printed state
stages.scope: Coptic/Arabic Euchologion: evening and morning incense, common order, three anaphoras and other prayers.
stages.summary: Contains Basil, Gregory and Cyril. The original Creed prints procession from the Father and the Son in both Coptic and Arabic. The Cyril section retains intercessions inside the anaphora. Brightman additionally describes revised commemorations including Chalcedon and extra Arabic rubrics.

evidence.locus: Title leaf 253291; incense openings 253295 and 253379; holding annotation
evidence.claim: Book identity, three anaphoras and incense offices confirmed.

evidence.locus: Printed lxvii, Coptic Liturgies / Ordo communis
evidence.claim: Explicitly characterizes Tuki’s Catholic rite and the changes listed.
Attributes Tuki’s text to a thirteenth-century Vatican manuscript, without identifying its shelfmark.
The Creed’s Spirit clause visibly includes the Father and the Son in both columns.

evidence.locus: Part II anaphora heading p. 272 / artifact 565; intercessions pp. 277, 282 and 287–290 / artifacts 570, 575, 580–583
evidence.claim: Petitions for Church, travellers and departed stand inside the separately headed Cyril anaphora.
Original Coptic-Arabic completion statement gives 13 June 1736.

evidence.locus: Part II pp. 85–87, Arabic right columns / artifact pages 378–380; passage.coptic-catholic-church.missale-copto-arabicum.1736-rome-tuki.creed-arabic
evidence.claim: Complete Arabic Creed component is independently checked and retained with explicit normalization; remaining Coptic and Arabic service text is not transcribed.

stages.limitations: Creed wording and the placement of sampled Cyril intercessions are directly image-checked. Their exact differences from Tuki’s unidentified manuscript exemplar remain uncollated. Chalcedon and omitted commemorations remain Brightman’s scholarly description; no specific removed name or pope addition is inferred. The native binding certifies the complete Arabic Creed only (139 normalized words on three pages), excluding parallel Coptic, rubrics and every other book division; it is not a complete Ordinary or missal.
stages.reception: Brightman expressly identifies Tuki and derivatives as the Coptic Catholic modified rite; no parish adoption date established.

stages.label: Catholic edition with intercession moved forward
stages.scope: Coptic-Arabic Euchologion and placement of the intercession relative to its anaphoras.
stages.witness_label: Hūlāǧī’l-kanīsat al-iskandariyya / Euchologion of the Alexandrian Church, Cairo 1898
stages.summary: Lietzmann identifies the 1898 book and reports that the entire intercession, with multiple alterations, precedes all anaphoras.

evidence.claim: Describes the 1898 intercession arrangement in discussion of Mark/Cyril and Tuki 1736.

evidence.locus: Printed p. 4, Ausgaben der unierten Kopten, item 2
evidence.claim: Identifies the 1898 edition as Catholic.
Identifies Catholic Patriarchate publication in 1898 and a modified re-edition of Tuki’s 1736 text.

stages.limitations: Original 1898 title, pagination and revised prayer wording not yet inspected. 1898 is an attested publication state, not necessarily when relocation first occurred.
stages.reception: Chaîne identifies the Catholic Patriarchate as publisher; Hammerschmidt independently lists this as a Catholic edition. Dates of actual local adoption are not established.

stages.label: Aksumite collection’s preserved Eucharistic order
stages.date_label: Extant codex: thirteenth century or earlier; exact range unresolved
stages.scope: Euchologion ff. 46r–62v; Mark anaphora ff. 54rb–56va within UM-039.
stages.witness_label: Sinodos of Qǝfrǝyā, C3-IV-71/C3-IV-73, Ethio-SPaRe UM-039
stages.summary: Preserves an archaic Ge’ez Eucharistic collection with Mark. The source distinguishes an early translation layer from the substantially later surviving codex.

evidence.claim: Codex dated thirteenth century or earlier; translations assigned to fifth–sixth, latest seventh century; Euchologion and Mark loci identified.

stages.limitations: Unpositioned because the copy’s lower dating bound is unresolved. Fifth–seventh century is translation dating, not the manuscript date. No direct path to 1945 demonstrated.
stages.reception: Ancestral Ethiopian witness; neither modern Catholic adoption nor whole missal use demonstrated.

stages.label: Ethiopian liturgy printed in Rome with the New Testament
stages.date_label: Rome, 1548 (title and printer’s colophon); afterword dated 1549
stages.scope: Ge’ez Ordo communis with the anaphora of the Apostles, followed by the anaphoras of Our Lord and of Mary, printed after the Gospels and Acts.
stages.witness_label: Testamentum Novum … Missale cum benedictione incensi cerae et c. (Rome: Valerius and Ludovicus Doricus of Brescia, 1548; afterword 1549); Google copy jXZRAAAAcAAJ
stages.summary: The liturgical section opens on f. 158r under the Latin heading INTROITVS MISSE. New sections begin on f. 168r with the anaphora of Our Lord and on f. 170r with the anaphora of Our Lady Mary attributed to Abba Heryaqos (Cyriacus) of Behnesa; a further section opens on f. 174r. A Latin printer’s colophon dated 1548 closes the section on f. 176v, and Romans begins on f. 177r.

evidence.claim: Names the Missale with the blessing of incense and wax, printed through Fr. Petrus Ethyops with the help of pious persons under Paul III and the emperor Claudius, Anno M.D.XLVIII.

evidence.locus: f. 158r; headings ff. 168r and 170r; ornament band f. 174r
evidence.claim: Liturgical section opening and the two named anaphora headings are directly visible.

evidence.locus: f. 176v Latin colophon; PT1 Latin afterword
evidence.claim: The printers and Rome 1548 are named at the end of the liturgical section; the afterword dates the completed work 1549 (Ethiopian 6586) and names Tasfa Ṣeyon and his helpers.
The Latin preface presents the Ethiopians as devoted to the Roman Church while noting that they keep rites the universal Church has abrogated; it contains no approval of the liturgical text.

stages.limitations: Section headings and paratext only; the Ge’ez prayers are not transcribed or compared with UM-039, later manuscripts or the Catholic printings. The section starting on f. 174r is unidentified. The printing date is the book’s; it does not date the composition of any anaphora. Only the INTROITVS MISSE heading was read at f. 158r; identifying ff. 158r–167v as the Ordo communis with the anaphora of the Apostles follows Hammerschmidt (inventory source geez-hammerschmidt-anaphoras-preview), not a heading on the page.
stages.reception: Printed in Rome under papal patronage by an Ethiopian monk of Santo Stefano; no approbation, imprimatur or Roman revision is printed on the inspected leaves, and no use by a Catholic community is evidenced. The Propaganda Fide college ex libris shows later Roman ownership only.

stages.label: Vatican Catholic missal with seventeen anaphoras
stages.date_label: 1945: publication reported by scholarly and local ecclesial sources
stages.scope: Catholic Ge’ez missal: anaphora repertoire, source-described invocation and institution revisions, and later replacement.
stages.witness_label: Missale aethiopicum, Roman edition of 1945; original title page not acquired
stages.summary: Keren’s study reports expansion from fourteen to seventeen anaphoras and compares an altered Spirit invocation. Fritsch separately reports institution-narrative revisions in the Lord and James of Sarug anaphoras. These describe different changes.

evidence.locus: p. 1 introduction and sections (a)–(b); p. 2 section (c)
evidence.claim: Explicitly attributes these bounded revisions to the 1945 Vatican edition.

evidence.locus: PDF p. 5 table; p. 8 paragraph and prefatory quotation
evidence.claim: Compares 1890/1913 and 1945 invocation wording; reports three added anaphoras and fourteen becoming seventeen.

evidence.locus: PDF p. 2, arrowed paragraph preceding 1990–91 committee
evidence.claim: Identifies the Vatican 1945 missal as the literal translation base.
Provides a fuller Latin title and the Roman first-edition designation.
Identifies the 1945 edition as the book replaced by the new 2024 edition.

stages.limitations: No complete 1945 book acquired; exact prayer pages and approval act remain missing. The Keren table is not original-page collation, and does not show an earlier absence of every Spirit invocation. Added James brother of the Lord must not be confused with Fritsch’s revised James of Sarug.
stages.reception: The Keren bishop’s 2009 account identifies the 1945 edition as the base of the Blin translation. This establishes bounded reception in Eritrea; universal use and implementation dates remain unproved.

stages.label: Joint 2024 Catholic edition with chant annotations
stages.date_label: 2024 edition; editorial note 27 September 2024; presented 27 May 2025
stages.scope: Joint Ge’ez missal: ordinary, seventeen anaphoras, clarified rubrics and integrated chant notation.
stages.witness_label: Missal in the Ge’ez language (The new 2024 edition), Valore Italiano, ISBN 979-12-81584-24-2
stages.summary: The signed editorial note names 1945 as the replaced edition. Public native contents list seventeen anaphoras; the publisher’s opening prayer image shows chant notation. The 2025 ceremony is a presentation, distinct from the book’s stated edition year.

evidence.locus: Paragraph beginning For the first time; bishop interviews
evidence.claim: Reports chant novelty and the bread instruction; describes intended shared Catholic use.

evidence.locus: Il lavoro frutto di due commissioni
evidence.claim: Reports work on ancient sources and updating in relation to Vatican II and CCEO.

evidence.locus: Unnumbered editorial note, paragraphs 2–3 and dated signature
evidence.claim: Dates the edition 2024, explicitly replaces 1945, and describes joint revision, clarified rubrics and integrated musical notation.

evidence.locus: Preview 05 (contents), preview 07 (numbered anaphora list), preview 09 (opening prayer)
evidence.claim: Seventeen anaphoras are listed; Apostles starts p. 82, Lord p. 98, James of Sarug p. 324; chant marks are visible in the opening prayer.

stages.limitations: Only public preview leaves inspected; no complete native book or institution narratives. The 2024 note and 2025 presentation do not establish an approval or effective date. The bread instruction is not proved new; retention/reversal of 1945 institution edits is unknown.
stages.reception: Prepared jointly for Ethiopian and Eritrean Catholic Churches at their hierarchs’ request. May 2025 bishop interviews express implementation hopes; universal adoption and local start dates remain unestablished.

stages.label: Keren Catholic Ge’ez missal
stages.scope: Catholic Ge’ez printing with fourteen anaphoras; source-described prayer passage.
stages.witness_label: Keren 1890 printing; no original copy acquired
stages.summary: Coulbeaux’s Keren printing contains fourteen anaphoras.

evidence.claim: Identifies this printing and compares one prayer passage with 1945.
English account identifies place, year and Catholic editorial context.

stages.limitations: Original title, index, approval and prayer pages remain unavailable. The retrospective table is source-described evidence, not direct collation.
stages.reception: Catholic mission printing in present-day Eritrea; no claim of uniform reception or present ecclesial boundaries.

stages.label: Asmara Catholic Ge’ez missal approved by Propaganda Fide
stages.date_label: Approbation 25 February 1913; imprimatur Asmara 12 April 1913; imprint Ethiopian year ፲፱፻፯ (1914/15)
stages.scope: Catholic Ge’ez missal with fourteen anaphoras; Latin approbation and Eritrean imprimatur; one inspected prayer (the Apostles anaphora’s anamnesis and Spirit petition).
stages.witness_label: ሥርዓተ፡ ቅዳሴ፡ ዘቤተ፡ ክርስቲያን፡ ካቶሊካዊት፡ እንተ፡ በኢትዮጵያ። (Asmara, Catholic press, Ethiopian year ፲፱፻፯); ULB Bonn copy
stages.summary: The original book is now inspected. Propaganda Fide for Oriental Rite affairs approved the Missale Aethiopicum on 25 February 1913 as duly revised and purged of errors, for priests using the rite received in Abyssinia; the Vicar Apostolic of Eritrea gave the imprimatur at Asmara on 12 April 1913. The title-page imprint year is Ethiopian 1907. The Apostles anaphora asks the Father to send the Holy Spirit and power at the receiving of the bread and cup and, in the second person, to make it the Body and Blood.

evidence.locus: PDF p. 10, title page and imprint
evidence.claim: Native title, Asmara Catholic press and Ethiopian imprint year ፲፱፻፯ are directly visible.

Approbation dated Rome 25 February 1913 (Gotti, prefect; Rolleri, secretary) for priests of the rite received in Abyssinia, with the formula rite revisum et mendis expurgatum; imprimatur Asmara 12 April 1913 (Carrara, Vicar Apostolic of Eritrea).

evidence.locus: PDF pp. 44–45, anaphora of the Apostles: institution narrative, anamnesis and Spirit petition (left column foot of PDF p. 45 continuing at top of right column)
evidence.claim: The petition reads, in second-person address to the Father, that he send the Holy Spirit and power at the receiving of this bread and cup and make it (ወትረስዮ) the Body and Blood; a red rubric then directs a threefold blessing of bread and cup.
Identifies this printing and compares one prayer passage with 1945.
English account identifies place, year and Catholic editorial context.

stages.limitations: Original title, approval and one prayer are inspected; whole-book collation with 1890 is impossible without that book. Printed page numerals at the anaphora are not securely legible, so loci are PDF pages. The approbation’s claim of revision is unquantified. The Keren studies’ 1913 matches the approbation year; no separate 1913 impression is evidenced, so the stage’s publication bounds follow the imprint (1914/15).
stages.reception: Roman approbation for the priests of the rite received in Abyssinia and an Eritrean vicar apostolic’s imprimatur are directly evidenced. Use in Ethiopian, as distinct from Eritrean, territory and dated local adoption are not established.

stages.label: Roman Euchologion receiving common ritual directions

stages.witness_label: خولاجي كنيسة الإسكندرية, Rome 1971; original volume not acquired
stages.summary: The church’s bibliography identifies the 1971 Roman book. Its synod history reports incorporation of the common directions prepared in connection with the 1957 synod. A comparative article cites cup-narrative pages for Basil, Gregory and Cyril.

evidence.claim: Names title, Rome 1971 and Patriarch Stephanos I’s order.
Reports common ritual directions for the three anaphoras incorporated in the 1971 book.

evidence.locus: Sixth section, Coptic Catholic books, item 3
evidence.claim: Cites Cyril p. 627, Gregory p. 498 and Basil p. 305 in the 1971 edition.

stages.limitations: Official retrospective descriptions, not original-book collation. Exact changes to preceding rubrics and the authorizing instrument remain uninspected. The 1934 two-anaphora title does not prove that Cyril was suppressed in Catholic use.
stages.reception: Described as a Coptic Catholic patriarchal book. Publication and reported synodal reception do not establish adoption dates in individual parishes.

transitions.summary: Lietzmann’s comparison identifies a later printed arrangement in which the entire intercession is placed before all anaphoras, with alterations to its text.

changes.before: Intercessions for the Church, travellers and departed occur within Tuki’s separately headed Cyril anaphora.
changes.after: Entire intercession, with several alterations, placed before all the anaphoras in Cairo 1898.
changes.locus_before: Tuki 1736 part II: heading p. 272, sampled intercessions pp. 277, 282 and 287–290 (artifact pages 565, 570, 575, 580–583).
changes.locus_after: Cairo 1898: exact page not yet verified; arrangement described in Lietzmann p. 12.

evidence.claim: Explicitly describes 1898 relocation and multiple changes.
Original before-state placement directly checked; the 1898 after-state remains scholarly described.
Source-described change between named textual/printed states.
Both 1736 and 1898 are Catholic editions.
Author who used the 1898 text explicitly describes it as a modified re-edition of Tuki 1736.

transitions.limitations: The original 1736 placement is checked at bounded pages, while the 1898 relocation and re-edition’s dependence on Tuki remain scholarly descriptions by Lietzmann and Chaîne. The mixed comparison is therefore classified at scholarly-description level. Exact altered words and the date when relocation first entered the line remain unproved.

transitions.summary: The 2024 signed editorial note explicitly replaces the 1945 edition and reports integrated musical notation; the 2025 official report calls these annotations a first inclusion.

changes.before: The 1945 predecessor is named by the new book; the official presentation describes annotations as first included, but the earlier score pages remain uninspected.
changes.after: The 2024 edition integrates chant notes, visible in its public opening-prayer preview.
changes.locus_before: No 1945 page available; identification in 2024 editorial note paragraph 2, novelty in Vatican News 27 May 2025.
changes.locus_after: 2024 unnumbered editorial note paragraph 3; publisher preview 09, Prayer of the Covenant opening (section starts p. 11 in preview 05).

evidence.claim: Names replaced edition and integrated chant notes.
Native musical notation is visibly integrated.
Calls chant annotations a first inclusion.
Explicit replacement statement connects 1945 and 2024 at editorial-description level.
Describes the chant novelty.

transitions.limitations: Declared replacement is established at editorial-description level; no text collation, canonical effective date or proof of universal implementation. No claimed bread-rubric novelty or continuity of 1945 institution texts.

transitions.summary: Keren’s account describes an Asmara reprinting after the 1890 edition became unavailable.

evidence.claim: Reports the 1913 reprinting and unchanged fourteen-anaphora extent.
Explains reprinting after the earlier edition was out of stock.

transitions.limitations: This is attributed printing succession; neither whole-book identity nor absence of other textual changes is established. The inspected 1913 approbation calls the book duly revised and purged of errors, so a revision of unknown extent cannot be excluded; without the 1890 original no change can be named.

transitions.summary: The Keren study describes repertoire expansion and displays a bounded prayer-wording contrast between the earlier printing and 1945.

changes.before: The source reports fourteen anaphoras in 1890/1913.
changes.after: The source reports seventeen, adding Mary by Giyorgis, James brother of the Lord and Mark.

changes.locus_after: Keren history PDF p. 8; original 1945 index unavailable.

evidence.claim: Reports repertoire expansion and names the additions.

changes.after: The 1945 column separates an invocation over bread and cup, highlights ይረስዮ and prints cross marks.
changes.locus_before: Asmara book PDF p. 45, anaphora of the Apostles, foot of left column to top of right column (original page inspected 2026-10-21); Keren history PDF p. 5, middle column.
changes.locus_after: Keren history PDF p. 5, right column; original book page not supplied.

Identifies earlier printings, a native-script comparison and the expanded repertoire.
Approved original of the earlier printing; the sampled before-state is checked on the page.
